newsitem.title: GERMANY: German media poke fun at Bonn "wild dance".
newsitem.headline: German media poke fun at Bonn "wild dance".

text.p: German newspapers on Tuesday poked fun at the government over its row with the Bundesbank over revaluing the country's gold reserves and one newspaper said Bonn was in a "wild dance" to cure its budget troubles.
The mass-circulation Bild newspaper said it was "the dance around Bonn's billion (mark) hole" and that crisis talks led by Chancellor Helmut Kohl had failed to make any progress.
"At the end (of the talks) there was one agreement - that there was no agreement," the newspaper said.

The left-leaning Frankfurter Rundschau had a front-page cartoon portraying the Bundesbank as a cloud raining down gold on Finance Minister Theo Waigel dressed as an old woman with her apron open to catch the bars of gold.

Waigel and the Bundesbank are at odds over his plan to revalue the central bank's gold and currency reserves and use the booked profits to reduce Bonn's debt and help Germany meet entry criteria for the single European currency.
The Bundesbank has repeatedly warned Bonn against resorting to tricks designed to squeeze Germany into currency union, which is slated to begin on January 1, 1999.

The conservative Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung took a more serious tone in an editorial on Tuesday, saying "international investors were fleeing Europe" over the Bonn-Bundesbank dispute and the left-wing victory in France's run-off election.
"They worry that currency union, if it ever comes, will likely start with many members and will be soft," the newspaper said.
"Above all in the eyes of foreign investors, Germany has lost its credibility and weakened its negotiating position in European poker."

The Boersen Zeitung called those in charge of European monetary union "clueless acrobats" and predicted currency union would be delayed and Bonn's attempts to revalue the Bundesbank's gold would also be delayed.
